what: Designs the chips that train and run AI. Profits swing with the data center build-out.
how_valued: Next year profit from analysts, about 70% of it becomes free cash. Cyclical rate (yield + 5.25%) because demand comes in waves. Growth capped at 15%: today's growth is the top of a cycle, not the average.
watch: Data center revenue, gross margin, receivables vs sales, customer concentration
sanity_check: Forward P/E vs its own 5 year average

what: Makes chips or the machines that make them. Near monopolies, but they spend a lot on factories and follow the chip cycle.
how_valued: Cash share 60 to 90% (capex eats the rest). Normal rate for a monopoly with net cash (ASML), cyclical for Taiwan risk (TSMC). Growth from the middle of the cycle, not the peak.
watch: Orders and backlog, capex of the big customers, export rules, gross margin
sanity_check: P/E vs history and EV/EBITDA vs peers

what: Sells memory chips at prices set by supply and demand. Big profits at the top, losses at the bottom.
how_valued: Never values the peak: uses a normal year of profit and the risky rate (yield + 6.25%). Morningstar's long view helps because it looks through the cycle.
watch: Memory prices, gross margin, new capacity from Samsung and SK Hynix
sanity_check: Price to book and P/E on normal profit

what: A company trying to fix itself. Today's profit says little about the future.
how_valued: Low cash share (heavy investment), risky rate, growth capped at 15%. Morningstar weighs a lot because my DCF starts from a small profit. Needs a big margin of safety (35%).
watch: Gross margin, outside customers, cash burn, new shares sold
sanity_check: Price to book and price to sales

what: Huge networks (search, cloud, software, ads) that customers find hard to leave. AI spending is now very large.
how_valued: Normal rate. Cash share only 50 to 70% because data centers eat the profit. If the AI spending pays off, that share goes up and the fair price with it: that is the main upside.
watch: Cloud growth, capex vs operating cash flow, margins, AI revenue
sanity_check: P/FCF and forward P/E vs history

what: Sells devices and services to people. Very loyal customers, slower growth.
how_valued: Normal rate, cash share near 100%. Growth around 8 to 10%. The fair price is usually below the market price because the market pays a premium for safety.
watch: Services growth, iPhone units, buybacks, app store rules

what: Growing very fast and priced for it. Most of the value is far in the future.
how_valued: Risky rate, growth capped at 15%, so my DCF is far below the price. Morningstar (40%) gives the long view. Expect these to look expensive most of the time and wait for a crash.
watch: Revenue growth, operating margin, stock pay, customer count
sanity_check: EV/sales and the growth the price needs (reverse DCF)

what: Subscriptions that renew every year. High margins, but AI agents could change who wins.
how_valued: Cash share 80 to 100%. Normal or cyclical rate. Growth from subscription growth. Free cash flow is higher than profit because of stock pay, so I use profit to stay conservative.
watch: Subscription growth, backlog (cRPO), net retention, stock pay

what: Software that protects companies. Spending keeps growing, and big platforms are taking share from small vendors.
how_valued: Cash share near 100% (prepaid subscriptions). Very high uncertainty for most, so extra buys need 35% below fair. Growth capped at 15% even if revenue grows 20%+.
watch: ARR growth, net retention, free cash flow margin, big outages

what: Software with slow growth but lots of cash. Cheap if the business does not shrink.
how_valued: Normal rate, low growth (about 5%), cash share near 100%. The value is the cash it makes today.
watch: Revenue trend, customers leaving, cash returned

what: Equipment and power for data centers and the electricity grid. Long order books, cyclical.
how_valued: Cyclical rate. Cash share up to 100% (customer down payments help today). Vistra uses free cash per share because profit is noisy.
watch: Orders and backlog, margins, power prices, rules in Texas

what: Takes a small fee on every card payment. Little capital needed, steady growth.
how_valued: Normal rate, cash share 100%, growth around 12%. Rarely cheap: patience pays here.
watch: Payment volume, cross border travel, fee laws

what: Drug makers. Value depends on patents and the pipeline.
how_valued: Normal rate, cash share 75% while it builds factories. Growth capped at 15% even with the obesity drugs.
watch: Sales of key drugs, prices, pipeline results, patent dates

what: Aircraft engines and parts. Most profit comes from spare parts for 30 years after each sale.
how_valued: Normal rate, cash share near 100%, growth around 11%.
watch: Deliveries, spare parts, Airbus and Boeing production rates

what: Medical robots or devices with recurring sales of tools and service.
how_valued: Normal rate, cash share 85 to 95%, growth from procedures.
watch: Procedure growth, new systems placed, recalls
